hero.title: Do sovereign-citizen tricks work? In court, no, and they usually make things worse.
hero.lede: Right to travel, the strawman, accepted for value, UCC 1-308, state national papers, land patents, the 1871 corporation: promoters on YouTube and in blogs sell these as ways to escape licences, taxes, debts and courts. This page collects what those sources claim and checks each claim against court rulings, statutes, government notices and research on the movement.

recap.bottomLine: none of the pseudolegal theories survives contact with the courts. Judges and appeal courts in the US, Canada and Australia reject the right to travel without a licence, the strawman, redemption and accepted-for-value bills, UCC 1-308 signatures, land patents and the 1871 corporation story, and people who rely on them tend to end up with more charges, penalties or lost homes. The people who reliably gain are the teachers who sell the seminars and kits. {hypeWrong} of {hypeTotal} sweeping promises ("secret account", "never pay again", "cannot be detained") are judged wrong.
